key_insight: A precision-first, physics-checked literature pipeline builds electro-optic datasets that support property prediction for unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: The approach could guide electro-optic material selection for optical modulators and microwave-to-optical quantum links.
method: Acquire relevant literature and extract records using layout-aware LLMs and deterministic table parsers.
Apply three-tier verification, symmetry checks, notation normalization, and provenance tracking.
Consolidate cross-paper values with robust statistics and audit a noise-robust surrogate using leave-one-material-out testing.
evidence_signal: From 49 papers, 414 of 816 candidates were accepted; exact-match precision/recall were 0.51/0.48 against 303 gold-standard values, while held-out materials beating a mean baseline increased from 1/4 to 9/13 across database snapshots.
watch_item: Despite the precision-first design, exact-match accuracy remains limited, and the improving prediction trend is not a controlled comparison.
paper_title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
